neighbours.label: the word 'awkward' (and its piece 'ward' after 'awk'), any context
fire: There was an awkward silence after he forgot her name at the party.
The interview felt awkward because the manager kept checking his phone.
Teenagers often go through an awkward phase at around fourteen.
She gave an awkward laugh and quickly changed the subject.
Carrying the sofa up the narrow stairs was awkward and slow.
It was awkward to sit next to my ex at the wedding dinner.
The puppy took a few awkward steps across the slippery floor.
His speech ended on an awkward note that nobody knew how to answer.
quiet: There was a long silence after he forgot her name at the party.
The interview felt strange because the manager kept checking his phone.
Teenagers often go through a difficult phase at around fourteen.
She gave a nervous laugh and quickly changed the subject.
Carrying the sofa up the narrow stairs was hard and slow.
It was uncomfortable to sit next to my ex at the wedding dinner.
The puppy took a few clumsy steps across the slippery floor.
His speech ended on an odd note that nobody knew how to answer.

notes: Card: ' awkward' x23 of top 32, plus 'ward' in awk-ward and surname endings (Hubbard, Hayward).
